$comment: Large-payload probe raw record (dogfood section 8.11): tablet-notes-v3 --all x 2 repetitions. Metadata and adjudication only: no source content, no secrets. Server fields read from WorkspaceReviewLogEntry lines via the Vercel runtime-logs API; both runs matched by requestBytes 513338. The 400,000-byte snapshot content cap binds CLIENT-side in capture (bytewise path order), which is why droppedByServerCaps is 0 while zero Swift source reached the payload.
experimentLabel: size-ceiling retirement probe: 513 KB real-repo snapshot under the reka/fp4,makora default pin

capture.contentCompositionNote: The client-side 400,000-byte cap filled in bytewise path order with .claude/, App Store materials, docs and config; no Swift or JavaScript application source reached the payload. Both reviews independently state this.

runs.findingsNote: All four findings are documentation-level (committed key flagged by the repo's own docs, App Store description overclaiming encryption, two stale docs); none touch application code, because none was in the payload.

verdictFlap: Byte-identical payloads returned verdict pass (0 findings) and verdict findings (4) — the section 8.5.3 instability observed at the VERDICT level on a real repository. A consumer gating on verdict alone would flip between runs.
conclusion: Delivery is size-independent well past the old ceiling: 513 KB / 99,610 input tokens completed in 3.9 s and 6.2 s on attempt 1 under the pinned provider. Phase B's 0-for-4 at 43 KB is now fully attributed to the pre-tuning provider/reasoning regime, not payload size. The binding problem at this size is TER-43: capture's bytewise-path-order fill produced a review of documentation instead of source.
